The general public frequently misunderstands different diet strategies because it's full of dimwits and, even worse, midwits with delusions of intelligence. Both groups are prone to binary thinking: i.e. low carb diets work because carbs must be "bad."

In reality, low carb diets work because they are an effective counter to the average American diet which is full of fried batter, starchy snacks, and insane amounts of sugar. You can't eat any of that on a low carb diet and thus these fatasses end up halving their daily calorie intake and actually lose weight for once.

Basic nutrition science is easy: all your calories are derived from fat (9 calories/gram), carbs (4 calories/gram), and protein (4 calories/gram). Low fat diets were promoted in the past because fat gave you the most calories per unit. Laying off fat would therefore provide more calorie restriction and more weight loss.

However, this doesn't make fat "bad" either; it's still a macronutrient needed by the human body. Humans, in fact, crave fat. Fat is why fried food tastes better than boiled food. Fat is why beef tastes better than chicken. White meat chicken is almost pure protein with very little fat, which is why it has very little flavor and why so many other lean meats are said to "taste like chicken."

An actual balanced diet is something like a gram of protein per pound of lean body mass with the rest of your calories more or less balanced between carbs and fat. Different body types and genetics have different needs. Regardless, eating low protein while losing weight is why people end up skinny fat. Your body loses fat during weight loss but it also eats up lean muscle tissue. Eating protein (and weightlifting) will have a muscle sparing effect. This is why bodybuilders end up cut for summer while the office drones on the treadmill end up skinny except for their beer belly.
